what.question: What is MyrmAgent?
what.answer: MyrmAgent is an AI agent platform with a persistent sandbox, memory system, and GUI-first interface. It helps you research, code, and automate tasks without managing infrastructure.

pronounce.question: How do you pronounce MyrmAgent?
pronounce.answer: /ˈmɜːrm ˈeɪdʒənt/. Myrm comes from the Greek word for ant — the same root as myrmecology and our Colony Agents multi-agent metaphor.

local.question: Can I use my own API keys?
local.answer: Yes. Bring Your Own Key (BYOK) is supported — you pay your LLM provider directly for those calls while still using the full MyrmAgent workspace.

data.question: Where is my data stored?
data.answer: Your workspace data stays in an isolated environment under your control — persistent memory, files, and sessions are not shared with other users. See our Privacy Policy for details.

embedWindow.question: How is retrieval quality guaranteed for long or multi-language documents?
embedWindow.answer: MyrmAgent auto-detects your embedding model's input window and derives a chunk budget matched to its tokenizer family — character-based for BERT/wordpiece models (BGE, MiniLM, E5…) to prevent silent truncation of Chinese/Japanese/Korean text. Any input that still exceeds the window fails loudly before the embedding API is called, so retrieval quality never degrades without warning.

cloudResources.question: Do I get exactly the sandbox resources my plan promises?
cloudResources.answer: Yes — every paid tier maps to a concrete container profile (CPU, memory, disk, and process limits) that is applied automatically and verified at creation, so what you pay for is exactly what runs. The Doctor panel also shows two-level process-saturation alerts (70% warn / 90% fail) before a busy sandbox ever freezes silently.

optionalExtras.question: Do I need to install every Python package manually?
optionalExtras.answer: No for most workflows. Channel SDKs (Matrix, Discord, Feishu) install on-demand from Settings with no restart. Optional skill bundles—such as WeChat article formatting—use named extras (`uv sync --extra wechat-formatter`) so Desktop stays lean while Docker can ship `--all-extras`. Missing packages surface honest install hints instead of silent mid-task failures.

highlightsCarousel.title: One workspace for all your AI work
highlightsCarousel.subtitle: Memory, safety, goals, channels, and teamwork — built for daily use, not a spec sheet.

aiWorkstation.label: Your workstation
aiWorkstation.title: Not a chatbot. Not an IDE plugin. Your AI workstation.
aiWorkstation.desc: Memory, skills, agents, channels, full GUI — two minutes to first task. Six-locale WebUI with CI parity gates; Saved Agent output locale SSOT (e.g. Korean formal 합니다体) survives Goal turn 2+ — OpenClaw/Hermes have UI or docs i18n only, not agent runtime honorifics. Hermes / OpenClaw users: GUI migration wizard with dry-run — no terminal required.

agentSandbox.label: Agent in sandbox
agentSandbox.title: Hard work runs isolated — your machine stays yours
agentSandbox.desc: Long runs stay in an isolated sandbox—you get a summary, not chaos. Agents can actively read workspace screenshots and videos (semantic glance/OCR/two-image compare + pixel diff) without you re-uploading files; video uses a dedicated vision model slot with a vlm/native_video/frame badge in chat. Background Tasks panel lists every shell with one-click Cancel. Artifacts preview in-app; 70+ pre-installed libraries for reports and analysis.

memoryKnowsYou.label: Memory & wiki
memoryKnowsYou.title: Eight memory types that learn you over time
memoryKnowsYou.desc: Eight memory types learn your preferences across sessions. Incognito when you need privacy; enable Wiki + Memory together for unified recall in one tool call—long articles stay in Wiki, short facts stay in Memory (automatic write guards when both are on). After answers, tap Memory N to see which memories grounded the reply—citations survive reload. Type @wiki: to inject specific wiki concepts. Per-agent wiki vaults in Settings keep each agent's documents isolated, featuring a Typora-grade split-pane Markdown live-preview editor and unsaved draft protection to prevent accidental loss. Wiki pages enforce a frontmatter `type` contract at compile and review—Repair Page Types fixes legacy notes in one click. After compile or import, Settings Overview shows the Karpathy-style index/log/hot cognitive map readiness and zero-LLM structural health badges (broken links, wikilinks, missing types) that refresh when you edit concepts. Bulk ingest streams live progress over SSE; the External Sources card pulls Gmail labels and RSS into your vault on a schedule—pull phase uses no AI credits. Every recall is wall-clock time-guarded across memory, wiki, conversation history and web corpora: if a corpus ever hangs or slows down, search fails open in seconds with a graceful degraded notice instead of stalling your conversation. A Brand Style board in Settings lets you define your brand identity (colors, fonts, tone, taboos) once—it is stably injected into every session so AI-generated copy, design and documents automatically match your brand.

memoryPoisonGuard.label: Memory safety
memoryPoisonGuard.title: Every memory write passes security & trust screening
memoryPoisonGuard.desc: Hidden instructions inside malicious webpages, documents or emails can't sneak into your long-term memory even if they fool the conversation; API keys, passwords and SMS codes are sanitized before persistence. Manual stores, batch writes, memory updates, user profile, rules, the MCP tool, agent auto-extraction and import recovery—all nine write paths share one guard, and a CI poisoning benchmark gate keeps it from regressing. Every memory also passes nine layers of trust verification—guesses and unconfirmed inferences never masquerade as facts, and stale, contested or unsupported facts are automatically down-weighted at recall so your answers stay grounded in what's actually true. Your memory belongs to you.

memoryStorageResilience.label: Memory resilience
memoryStorageResilience.title: No matter how full, slow or fragile the disk gets, memory never breaks
memoryStorageResilience.desc: Memory persists in a local embedded vector store—zero Docker dependency, works out of the box. When disk space runs out, a directory is occupied, or permissions tighten, memory automatically switches to in-memory mode and keeps reading and writing—no interruption, returning to persistence automatically once the disk recovers. Retrieval never hangs either: if any memory corpus stalls or slows down, the search times out on schedule and degrades gracefully, and the agent is honestly told "search timed out — try a more specific query or retry" across both the GUI and MCP surfaces—a failed retrieval is never disguised as "no memory", so it never fabricates answers. Every path is a process-wide singleton, so concurrent agents never hit file-lock conflicts or corruption; throwaway memory volumes for evals and workspaces are burned after use with zero leaked file handles. Isolated volumes never cross-contaminate each other's data—your memory stays yours, never mixed, never leaked. And you can always see, at a glance in the Memory Command Center, whether memory is stored persistently, has fallen back to in-memory mode, or is unavailable—so "memory will be lost on restart" is never a silent surprise. Every critical state file—context snapshots, skill state, encryption keys, usage ledgers—is written via crash-consistent atomic write (temp file → fsync → atomic rename), so a crash or restart can never leave a half-written corrupted file: your data is always complete, never a fragment.
memoryStorageResilience.statLabel: memory lost on disk failure — zero leaks
memoryStorageResilience.tag1: Auto-degrade keeps memory running on disk failure
memoryStorageResilience.tag3: Isolated volumes burned after use, zero residue

deepResearch.label: Search & research
deepResearch.title: Deep research with local-first crawling
deepResearch.desc: Multi-engine search, local fetch, and cited reports—four source types with previews. Your wiki knowledge is automatically scanned before web searches, saving cost and avoiding redundancy; past reports are auto-archived and reused in future research, with built-in cross-validation of prior conclusions—no manual mode switching needed. Three-layer knowledge transfer: same-session chat history, cross-session Wiki auto-archiving with EXPLORE recall, and agent memory_recall tool for general conversations—research never gets lost. Comparison queries automatically generate plans with consistent evaluation dimensions and produce summary comparison tables. Review and edit the research plan before execution. Pause anytime; real-time per-cycle cost and budget visible. Dual-model architecture cuts research costs while keeping report quality high. End-to-end Research→Notes→Deck workflow: save reports to your wiki with one click, edit freely, then generate professional PPTs through natural conversation—more flexible than any fixed template engine. Cross-document analysis: upload multiple files and the agent identifies consensus, contradictions, and attributed quotes across documents—citations are clickable and jump to highlighted source text, with no limits on analysis angles. Unified output panel: mind maps (interactive Mermaid SVG with zoom/fullscreen/download), podcast audio (dual TTS engines), PPTs, HTML, and all artifact types in tab-switchable view—one click to save to Wiki.

desktopComputerUse.label: Silent Desktop Agent
desktopComputerUse.title: Working for you, never stealing your mouse
desktopComputerUse.desc: Background desktop automation without stealing focus. Semantic UI trees plus vision fallback—and guardrails for risky actions. Canvas/rich-editor visual mode: auto-detects Google Docs, Figma, Sheets and switches to coordinate-based interaction with humanized Bézier mouse trajectories. Just 3 tools cover everything competitors need 11 tools for—saving ~4,000 tokens per request in tool descriptions alone, so the agent decides faster and more accurately. Turn-end control is always released: whether the agent finishes, you stop it, it errors, or the budget runs out, the "controlling" indicator vanishes instantly — no lingering "AI stopped but the screen still says using computer" (a common complaint on competitor products). Python calls OS APIs directly—pip install and go, no compiling Rust/Swift native daemons, zero path conflicts. 548 backend + 10 frontend tests all green.

multiAgent.label: Multi-agent
multiAgent.title: Simple by default, a team on demand
multiAgent.desc: Default single-agent speed; Goal auto-continuation inherits the chat-bound Saved Agent profile (honorific suffix, team Leader protocol, subagent tools) — no profile drop on turn 2+. Flip one toggle to unlock 8 orchestration modes, Kanban self-claim dispatch, and live topology boards. Code-enforced DAG/Council/Verification orchestration replaces fragile Prompt-only workflows — 1,680 tests, 0 failures. Background subagents are fire-and-deliver: ending the parent message no longer kills wait=false async tasks, and completed results stay visible for 3600s after refresh; the Dashboard's dual-trust indicator (execution progress + verified state) shows everything on one screen.

omniChannel.label: Channels & automation
omniChannel.title: Same agent on chat, voice, and cron
omniChannel.desc: Chat, cron, and messaging from one agent—auto-adapts reply style per channel (concise on mobile IM, detailed on desktop); send commands remotely via WeChat/Telegram/Slack, one-tap approve risky actions without exposing your PC to the internet; completed/failed/blocked tasks push to your phone instantly — never 'discover next morning that a task hung all night'; quiet when nothing needs you.

tokenSmart.label: Token smart
tokenSmart.title: More work on the same API budget
tokenSmart.desc: 11-step context pipeline + zero-LLM rule compression (dedup, semantic output compression, image strip) on by default — far beyond Tokenomics Lite's single-layer 8–15%/turn; on-demand skill loading cuts fixed overhead; model-switch preflight shows compression risk before you send — long chats stay stable, savings visible in the health ring. Re-reading the same file never re-bills or breaks the cache — unchanged files return a lightweight stub instead of re-sending identical content, keeping long-session costs flat. Every call is counted too: sub-agents, workflows and background summaries all report into one honest ledger, so your bill never hides background spend.
tokenSmart.tag1: Zero-LLM rule compression · on by default
tokenSmart.tag2: Model-switch preflight — see compression risk before switching

evalLab.label: Eval Lab & Memory A/B
evalLab.title: Memory's value, proven with numbers, not hype
evalLab.desc: Eval Lab turns 'is my agent getting better?' into measurable, reproducible scores. Run the built-in WorkBuddy Bench — four realistic tracks (Code, Web, Office, Security) with checksum-verified downloads and live progress — and watch the agent execute real tests with pass rates scored from actual results, never an LLM judging itself. The killer proof: one-click Memory A/B runs the same tasks twice, memory on vs off, and reports side-by-side pass rates, token cost, and exactly how many memory tool calls happened — a real number honest enough to admit single-turn tasks benefit less. International benchmarks plug straight in: OpenAI BrowseComp (1,266 real questions) joins the same Eval Lab, and every report records both the scored agent model and the judge model, keeping numbers audit-proof. Each case runs in an isolated sandbox destroyed after the run — no cross-case file races, no disk buildup. Layered Evaluation runs the same tasks across an ascending harness chain — bare model, core harness, plus skills, plus memory — and reports each layer's measured gain. Integrity is engineered in: the agent is barred from Hugging Face and other answer-key repos so no benchmark can be gamed, each benchmark declares its own tool-call and iteration budget so stuck tasks stop automatically with the reason marked, and every report shows blocked attempts and which limit stopped the run.
evalLab.tag1: One-click Memory A/B — memory on vs off
evalLab.tag2: Scores from real tests, zero LLM judging · per-case isolated sandbox, destroyed after run
evalLab.tag3: Layered eval quantifies each harness layer's gain · contamination-proof runs with declared budgets

memoryDoctor.label: Memory Doctor
memoryDoctor.title: Know when memory breaks — and when it gets slower
memoryDoctor.desc: One click runs a real memory check-up: your agent actually writes and re-reads 16 scenarios across 8 memory types, then scores recall quality and retrieval latency. Every result is archived, and the trend panel plots recall and P50/P95 latency over time — so “the agent feels slower” becomes a curve you can see, and the exact memory category regressing shows up immediately.
memoryDoctor.tag1: Recall quality + latency trends in one panel
memoryDoctor.tag3: Model-switch drift hints keep scores honest

voiceBgDone.label: Voice task closure
voiceBgDone.title: Speak, walk away — the agent speaks up when your task is done
voiceBgDone.desc: Dispatch a background task by voice (research, report, script), then leave the computer. When it finishes, the agent proactively tells you the result in your next voice session — symmetrically across all four voice modes (audio_only / agent_bridge / OpenAI Realtime / Gemini Live), so nothing is ever missed. Task finishes while the agent is mid-sentence? The completion announcement queues safely in the TTS pipeline and plays the moment it finishes speaking — it never interrupts what you're hearing. Multiple windows open? Session-scoped deduplication means only the active voice window announces, exactly once. The chat timeline refreshes in real time too, so when you want details you can just ask, and the agent answers with full context.
voiceBgDone.tag1: Proactive completion announcement with result summary
voiceBgDone.tag2: Queue-safe insertion — never interrupts current speech

i18nLocalization.label: Six languages, one agent
i18nLocalization.title: Every built-in agent speaks your language
i18nLocalization.desc: All 25 built-in agents are fully localized in 6 languages (EN / 中文 / 繁體 / 日本語 / 한국어 / DE) — names and job descriptions stay consistent across chat, kanban, memory, settings, and every dropdown, picker and @mention. No corner leaks raw English. Industrial-grade i18n gates in CI auto-block untranslated leaks and translation drift, so localization quality never decays release after release.
i18nLocalization.tag1: Names + descriptions across the full UI
i18nLocalization.tag2: CI gates block English leaks & drift

humanReview.label: Review, one tap away
humanReview.title: Tasks waiting for your call? See them globally, reach them instantly
humanReview.desc: Tasks that need a human sign-off (background jobs, cron, long-running deliverables) land in a 'pending review' state instead of pretending to be done. A global pending-review counter in the nav and fleet overview tells you, at a glance, how many items are waiting for your decision — no matter which project they belong to. Tap the notification or the counter and you're dropped straight into the board's in-review column; approve to complete and auto-advance dependents, or reject with a reason to send it back for rework. The count updates in real time — a complete number → action → result loop, so no human gate is ever missed.
humanReview.tag2: Tap notification to land in review
humanReview.tag3: Approve completes · reject sends back with reason

reasoningModel.label: Any model, stable answers
reasoningModel.title: Reasoning models included — answers survive, thinking stays out
reasoningModel.desc: DeepSeek-R1, Qwen-QwQ, OpenAI o-series, minimax M3 — models that put the final answer in reasoning_content instead of content are a silent trap for most agent frameworks: scripts, tool results, and UI end up empty or printing 'None'. Myrm extracts the user-visible answer through a model-agnostic layer that also strips <think> blocks and tolerates Anthropic block lists, so generated scripts, wiki articles, and structured results stay clean no matter which provider you plug in. It also parses structured JSON from raw model output — fenced code, prose-wrapped, even with stray control characters or trailing commas — through one self-repairing extraction layer shared by every skill, wiki, and memory pipeline, so nothing needs a manual retry. No per-model whitelist to wait for — new models just work.
reasoningModel.tag2: Robust JSON extraction (fences, prose, stray chars)

browserRecording.label: Record & replay browser work
browserRecording.title: Record a browser flow once — replay it as a reusable skill
browserRecording.desc: Click through a workflow in the recorder panel and Myrm turns it into an executable skill your agent can replay anytime — no scripting required. Recording is semantic, not raw: selects record both value and human-readable labels, multi-selects stay complete, form fields are disambiguated by their real labels (aria-label, label[for], wrapping label, placeholder), input-method composition never fragments Chinese/Japanese text, SPA route changes and redirect chains are folded automatically, and hover/Enter-submit steps are deduplicated. The generated skill is readable, token-lean, and replayable across sessions — record once, automate forever.

browserHealthOps.label: Browser health ops
browserHealthOps.title: One click diagnoses the browser stack — and cleans up orphan processes
browserHealthOps.desc: Run a full browser check-up right from Settings: engines, memory, disk, proxy and the extension relay are all probed for real and graded, with concrete fix suggestions for anything failing. Orphan Chromium/driver processes that survive crashes are detected machine-wide and cleaned up in one click behind a confirm gate — no more hunting PIDs in Activity Monitor. Your agent can also run a Core Web Vitals check on any page it visits — LCP, CLS and INP graded against Google's official thresholds, with the fix already suggested.
browserHealthOps.tag2: One-click orphan cleanup behind a confirm gate
browserHealthOps.tag3: Fix suggestion for every failing check

humanizedBrowsing.label: Browses like a person
humanizedBrowsing.title: Scrolls, clicks and moves like a human — invisible to anti-bot systems
humanizedBrowsing.desc: Every scroll is a real mouse-wheel input with human rhythm — acceleration, deceleration, natural pauses, tiny overshoots and corrections — never a tell-tale JavaScript one-shot jump. Clicks first wheel the target into view the human way, honest scroll feedback means the agent never claims a success it didn't achieve, and nested scroll containers and iframes are handled precisely.
humanizedBrowsing.tag1: Real wheel input, not JS jumps

skillGrowth.label: Evolution, quantified
skillGrowth.title: Skills get smarter every use — see exactly how much better
skillGrowth.desc: Myrm learns skills from real usage: examples, failures and feedback are distilled into reusable skills that repair and evolve themselves. Every evolution carries a before/after quality score badge right in the history panel, so you always know what changed and whether it actually improved. Fuzzy matching, regression-safe changes (verified not to break existing behavior), approve-before-apply and one-click rollback guard each step; the Growth Center unifies pending/approved/rejected reviews with real-time badge sync — your agent gets smarter every day, fully under your control.
skillGrowth.statLabel: quality score scale · before/after per evolution
skillGrowth.tag2: Unified review in Growth Center · realtime sync

interactiveUi.label: Interactive UI
interactiveUi.title: Results you can see, click, and drive — not Markdown to decode
interactiveUi.desc: While other agents dump code blocks, Myrm's agent renders live, interactive interfaces right in the chat — cards, charts, tables, forms and more. Data refreshes incrementally: progress bars tick, status badges flip, tables update in place, without re-sending the whole UI. Click a button or submit a form and the agent picks it up instantly and keeps going. The interface isn't a showpiece — it's a remote control for your agent.
interactiveUi.tag3: Form & button actions feed back to the agent

evidenceDiscipline.label: Honesty, enforced
evidenceDiscipline.title: Knows what it knows — and says so
evidenceDiscipline.desc: AI assistants fail in predictable ways: a command exits cleanly so it claims the service is fixed; a file is edited so it claims the feature works; it can check something itself but asks you to repeat it instead. Myrm's default agent ships with evidence discipline built in: it separates what it directly observed from what it inferred or what you told it, never upgrades a failed check or an empty result into a successful verification, bounds negative claims to what it actually checked, and verifies on its own before ever asking you to repeat information. No verification theater, no UNKNOWN as an excuse — results you can trust without re-checking.
evidenceDiscipline.tag1: Observed vs inferred vs user-reported — always distinguished
evidenceDiscipline.tag2: Never calls a failed check a success
evidenceDiscipline.tag3: Checks before it asks · bounded negative claims

marketplaceAgentInstall.label: Agent marketplace, safe upgrades
marketplaceAgentInstall.title: One package. Whole Agent. Undo any upgrade.
marketplaceAgentInstall.desc: Claude Code and Cursor force you to hand-assemble an agent: subagent YAML, plugins, MCP tools, skill bindings — four separate steps that drift apart. Myrm installs a complete Agent package in one atomic step (model + prompt + bundled skills + subagents + MCP + safety profile), remapping publisher IDs to your local store so bindings never dangle. When the cloud pushes a new version, empty package fields never overwrite your customizations, local skill/subagent bindings survive, a snapshot is written before every push, and a misbehaving upgrade rolls back with one click.
marketplaceAgentInstall.statLabel: atomic install · safe push · one-click rollback
marketplaceAgentInstall.tag1: Full Agent package: model · skills · subagents · MCP · safety
marketplaceAgentInstall.tag2: Upgrades never clobber local customizations or bindings
marketplaceAgentInstall.tag3: Snapshot before every push · undo any upgrade

rewindUndo.label: Rewind & undo, survives refresh
rewindUndo.title: Rewind conversations and file changes — even after refresh
rewindUndo.desc: Every agent turn snapshots the files it touches, and every message keeps a rewind point. Delete the messages after a wrong turn, or restore just the files that turn modified — pick individual files, not everything. The best part: rewind survives a page refresh. Message IDs, snapshot ownership and sandbox paths are wired so your undo button keeps working after reload, in parallel chats, and on cloud sandboxes. Competitor rewinds are CLI-session-scoped: close the page and your undo is gone.
rewindUndo.tag1: Undo a message, revert files, or roll back a whole session
rewindUndo.tag2: File diffs + selective per-file restore with confirm
rewindUndo.tag3: Survives refresh · works in cloud sandboxes

threeCeilingRead.label: Compiler-grade file reads
threeCeilingRead.title: Read any file without blowing up your context
threeCeilingRead.desc: Logs, CSVs, minified JS — other agents read these oversized or over-wide files and instantly eat your whole context window and token budget, sometimes handing back half a line of broken syntax. Myrm gates reads with three smart guardrails: a character budget, a line-count cap, and a per-line length cap. Anything beyond the limit is cut at a complete line boundary — never splitting a line of code — and you get a precise continuation offset, so reading on doesn't require guessing. Crucially, truncation happens at the display layer: the file on disk is left untouched, so post-read edit-integrity checks stay accurate. No faking the checks with edited content.
threeCeilingRead.tag1: Auto-guard oversized files · no token-bill blowouts
threeCeilingRead.tag2: Truncate at full line boundaries · never split syntax
threeCeilingRead.tag3: Precomputed resume offset · display-only, disk untouched

filePreview.label: In-app file preview
filePreview.title: Open any file without leaving the workspace
filePreview.desc: Click a PDF, image, video or audio file in the workspace browser and it renders in-app — no garbled text, no download first. The backend decides text vs binary (zero-IO extension detection), text is capped to keep the page snappy, and binary streams fully over HTTP Range. Downloads stay safe too: header injection is blocked and non-ASCII filenames encode via RFC 5987.

pdfSmartReading.label: Reads scanned PDFs
pdfSmartReading.title: No text layer? The agent reads it for you
pdfSmartReading.desc: Contracts, papers, old invoices — many critical PDFs are scans with images only, no text. Other agents either dump a pile of images for you to read yourself, or simply say "can't read it". Myrm's PDF toolchain auto-detects textless pages: renders them to images, runs local OCR page by page, and reassembles full text. @-mentions, knowledge-base imports and web-downloaded PDFs all hook in automatically — scanned files are no longer a blind spot, with zero cloud OCR dependency.
pdfSmartReading.statLabel: OCR wired into every text path · fully automatic
pdfSmartReading.tag1: Scanned PDF auto-OCR · no vision model needed
pdfSmartReading.tag3: Local OCR · data stays on-device · multilingual

mcpEcosystem.label: MCP ecosystem, plug & play
mcpEcosystem.title: 10,000+ MCP servers, zero config — the latest protocol, already shipped
mcpEcosystem.desc: Myrm speaks the newest MCP 2.0 protocol — a version ahead of other agents. It adopts SDK 2.x before anyone else: SSE stream leaks that plague long sessions are fixed, cloud deployments get stateless HTTP sessions, and tool errors arrive as structured data your agent actually understands instead of text to guess. Any MCP server in the ecosystem connects in seconds, in the browser, the desktop app, or your own private network.
mcpEcosystem.statLabel: MCP SDK generation · ahead of the ecosystem
mcpEcosystem.tag2: SSE leak fix · hours-long sessions stay stable
mcpEcosystem.tag3: Structured tool errors the agent can self-heal from

connectorDoctor.label: Connector Doctor
connectorDoctor.title: External-agent connections verified on disk — no more configure-and-pray
connectorDoctor.desc: Connecting Claude Code, Cursor, or any MCP client? Myrm's Doctor reads the client's actual config file on your machine — JSON or TOML, `~` expanded — verifies the `myrm-memory` entry exists and the Bearer token hash matches, then reports a machine-readable diagnosis with three-level severity (healthy / needs attention / failed). Wrong path, missing token, corrupted file, env-var placeholder: each gets its own clear code and fix guidance, in 6 languages. Tokens are stored as SHA-256 hashes only, and `${VAR}` placeholders are honestly flagged as unverifiable instead of misreported.
connectorDoctor.tag1: Reads the real on-disk config — JSON + TOML
connectorDoctor.tag2: Token hash verified · never stored in plaintext

permissionUsageStats.label: Skill permissions, on camera
permissionUsageStats.title: Every permission call is a dashboard, not a blind trust
permissionUsageStats.desc: Other agents make you trust third-party skills on faith — or drown you in per-request popups. Myrm logs every sensitive action a skill takes (write files, run commands, touch the network, read env vars) and turns it into a visual dashboard: total vs allowed vs denied per permission type, the exact denial reason, and the last 10 operations, filterable over 1/7/30/90-day windows. Spot at a glance when a skill tried to read environment variables thirty times and got denied every time. Revoke access in one click and the very next call is refused.
permissionUsageStats.statLabel: of sensitive skill calls logged & visualized
permissionUsageStats.tag3: One-click revoke · next call refused instantly

governanceGate.label: Tool governance
governanceGate.title: Every tool declared — no silent security bypass
governanceGate.desc: Other frameworks govern tools with manually maintained lists, so a newly added tool can silently fall back to 'ask every time' — or quietly lose capability. Myrm enforces a registration-level governance gate: every built-in tool must carry an explicit declaration (auto-allow for read-only, ask for risky, explicit fallback for high-risk) or the build fails. The gate cross-checks declarations against the real tool universe in both directions, so the security report can never contradict the code. High-risk tools keep an explicit human-confirmation baseline — nothing flips to auto-allow by accident.
governanceGate.tag1: CI-enforced: undeclared tool fails the build
governanceGate.tag3: Audit matrix matches code, or CI fails

failureFaultSide.label: Failure attribution
failureFaultSide.title: Task failed? Myrm tells you whose fault it is
failureFaultSide.desc: Other agents just throw a red error block when a task fails — was it a model hallucination, a broken tool, a misconfigured environment, or your own unclear instruction? You have to guess. Myrm's failure attribution engine classifies every failure deterministically into six sides — model / tool / pipeline / environment / grader / user. The live progress panel pins a fault badge on each failed step, the execution timeline keeps the root cause of past failures, and one-click recovery actions take you straight to the right fix — update API key, switch model, reinstall a dependency. Even when the problem is in your own instructions, it says so plainly instead of leaving you staring at a stack trace.
failureFaultSide.tag1: Instant fault attribution: model / tool / env / user

toolLineageAudit.label: Auditable AI actions
toolLineageAudit.title: Every tool call traced to its instruction — with the security verdict attached
toolLineageAudit.desc: Other agents treat tool calls as a black box — when something sensitive happens (a file edit, a command run, a network request), you can't tell which instruction caused it or whether the safety system even reviewed it. Myrm links every tool call back to the instruction that spawned it and attaches the security verdict to each step of the execution timeline. Replay any session: every sensitive action shows whether it was approved, denied, or flagged with a reason — so a 'works on my machine' claim is backed by an audit trail you can actually see, not a log you'd have to trust.
toolLineageAudit.statLabel: tool calls traced · security verdict per step
toolLineageAudit.tag1: Instruction → tool call → result, fully linked
toolLineageAudit.tag2: Approved / denied / flagged, each with a reason

enterpriseAgentAudit.label: Organization-wide audit
enterpriseAgentAudit.title: Every agent action across every team sandbox, on one auditable timeline
enterpriseAgentAudit.desc: In a real business, agents run in many sandboxes — how do you know what they all did, and whether anything slipped past your safety controls? Other agents have no answer: no cross-sandbox ledger, no way to say which member or sandbox a sensitive action belongs to, and failed scans are silently skipped. Myrm aggregates every tool call, approval, and security decision from all member sandboxes into one org-wide timeline: real deny counts (block/deny/redact/leak) are exact, each event is attributed to the right member and sandbox, and sandboxes that couldn't be scanned are surfaced instead of hidden. Audit coverage you can prove, not a log you have to trust.
enterpriseAgentAudit.statLabel: of sandboxes audited · org-wide deny count
enterpriseAgentAudit.tag1: All member sandboxes on one unified timeline
enterpriseAgentAudit.tag2: Real deny counts — block / deny / redact / leak
enterpriseAgentAudit.tag3: Unscannable sandboxes surfaced, never silently skipped

patternDiscovery.label: Memory, thinking
patternDiscovery.title: Your agent discovers the behavior patterns you haven't noticed
patternDiscovery.desc: Most memory systems just store what you said. Myrm goes one step further: every week it scans everything you've accumulated and surfaces the behavioral patterns you may not see yourself — recurring work habits, how your understanding of a topic evolved, unresolved threads that keep coming back, preference drift, blind spots. Each pattern comes with evidence, a confidence score, and a stability level; the most certain ones are automatically promoted into behavioral rules (with your approval) so your agent proactively applies the work preferences it learned from you. In the WebUI evolution review panel you can browse every pattern, expand its evidence, and trigger a fresh analysis anytime.
patternDiscovery.statLabel: auto analysis · patterns promoted to rules
patternDiscovery.tag1: Cross-session pattern discovery with evidence & confidence
patternDiscovery.tag2: High-confidence patterns auto-promote to rules (your approval)
patternDiscovery.tag3: WebUI evolution review panel — browse & trigger anytime

sessionPerfObservability.label: Per-response performance
sessionPerfObservability.title: See where every second and every dollar of a session went
sessionPerfObservability.desc: When a long task feels slow, other agents just make you wait — there is no way to tell whether the time went to thinking, tool calls, or a slow model, and no number for how long you actually waited for the first token. Myrm's session analytics breaks every session down by model: how many calls each model made and how long they took, plus a response-speed summary (average and P95 time-to-first-token). Open any session's analytics panel and you immediately see which model is your bottleneck and which reply was the slow one — data you can act on, instead of a feeling.
sessionPerfObservability.statLabel: time-to-first-token per session · LLM duration by model
sessionPerfObservability.tag1: LLM calls grouped by model with total duration
sessionPerfObservability.tag2: Response speed — avg & P95 first-token latency

streamResilient.label: No character left behind
streamResilient.title: Reconnect and resume — every character intact
streamResilient.desc: Other agents stream with diffs or naive chunking, so a dropped connection means dropped characters and reconnection is a gamble; on weak networks a slow client can pin the entire stream for everyone. Myrm's built-in stream buffer resumes exactly where you lost the connection using the standard SSE Last-Event-ID protocol — duplicates, gaps and reordering never happen. The Aug 2026 concurrency hardening means slow consumers (weak-network mobile) can no longer stall other clients, so several devices can watch the same live session without blocking each other.
